title: When I publish a new article on dev.to, I want to automatically republish it to my other platforms (
job_to_be_done: When I publish a new article on dev.to, I want to automatically republish it to my other platforms (Medium, personal blog, LinkedIn) with correct formatting, so I can save 30-60 minutes per article and ensure consistent cross-posting.
painful_workflow: Manually copy-pasting article content, reformatting Markdown, re-uploading images, and adjusting tags for each target platform after publishing on dev.to.
current_workaround: Copy-paste article content, reformat Markdown, re-upload images, and adjust tags for each target platform.
verified_facts: SIG-0001 documents at least one content creator manually copy-pasting, reformatting Markdown, re-uploading images, and adjusting tags to republish dev.to articles to Medium, personal blog, and LinkedIn (SIG-0001)
The claimed cost is 30-60 minutes per article plus formatting-error risk and inconsistent cross-posting (SIG-0001)
The pain recurs only per published article (SIG-0001)
The cluster is supported by a single independent source and a single source type (cluster metadata: independent_sources=1, source_type_count=1)
inferences: Most independent bloggers publish infrequently (weekly to monthly), so the pain likely fires only a few times per month

Free or near-free alternatives likely exist for this workflow (RSS-based importers, canonical-URL support, generic automation platforms, open-source cross-posting scripts), which would cap willingness to pay — this is market knowledge, not evidence from the cluster
The dev.to audience skews technical, making DIY scripting a realistic substitute for a paid product
The 30-60 minute estimate is plausible for multi-platform manual reposting but is unverified self-report
assumptions: The target user publishes often enough for the pain to matter — no cadence data exists in the cluster
The target user actually wants full-article cross-posting to LinkedIn rather than a link post, which is a niche behavior
The user has not already adopted an existing cross-posting tool or RSS-based import, which the evidence does not rule out
unknowns: Actual publishing frequency of the target persona
Whether the 30-60 minute figure is typical or an outlier
Whether any user has paid money or labor (e.g., hired a VA) to solve this
How many platforms the average user cross-posts to (pain scales with platform count)
Whether existing free tools already satisfy this need for most users
Market size: how many dev.to authors cross-post to 2+ other platforms
